units.title: Take medicines seriously
units.lesson: A surgical assessment starts with the person as well as the tooth. Relevant medical conditions, previous problems, allergies and current medicines belong in the history. Include prescribed medicines and products obtained without a prescription. Update the record when circumstances change. This chapter teaches what information matters; it does not recommend stopping or changing any medication.
units.question: Which item belongs in a current medication history?
choices: Only medicines from a hospital
Prescribed and non-prescription products
Only the last painkiller
units.explanation: A useful history includes prescribed and non-prescription products.
rationales: This is the more complete scope.

units.title: Consent is a discussion
units.lesson: Informed consent involves understanding the proposed care, its important risks and benefits, and alternatives. Relevant questions and the agreed decision should be documented. A signature records part of a process; it does not itself show that information was understood. This is a professional communication principle, not a complete statement of Indian consent law.
units.question: Which best represents informed consent?
choices: A discussion supporting an informed choice
A signature with no explanation
A promise of a guaranteed outcome
units.explanation: Information and an opportunity to decide are central.
rationales: A signature alone is insufficient evidence of understanding.

units.title: Separate patient and procedure risk
units.lesson: Bleeding risk is not a single label attached to a drug name. SDCEP distinguishes features of the planned procedure from patient factors, including medicines, other conditions and previous bleeding. These dimensions need consideration together. The UK guidance supplies this reasoning framework; this lesson gives no drug-interruption schedule or operative recommendation.
units.question: Which pair belongs in bleeding-risk reasoning?
choices: Shoe size and appointment colour
Drug name alone and nothing else
Patient factors and procedure-related risk
units.explanation: Both patient and procedure dimensions contribute.
rationales: These do not describe bleeding risk.
One label cannot represent the whole assessment.
units.hint: What is being done, and to whom?

units.title: Explain haemostasis
units.lesson: Haemostasis limits bleeding after vascular injury. Platelets contribute an initial plug; coagulation produces fibrin that helps stabilize the clot. These processes interact rather than act as unrelated systems. Distinguish platelet function from the fibrin-forming cascade when organizing theory. This distinction does not identify a patient’s bleeding disorder without appropriate assessment.
units.question: Which product helps stabilize a platelet plug?
choices: Fibrin
Enamel
Keratin
units.explanation: Fibrin forms a reinforcing clot network.
rationales: Keratin is a structural epithelial protein.

units.question: A paper history lists medical diagnoses but no medicines. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: No medication is being taken
The medication record remains incomplete
The diagnoses reveal every current medicine
units.explanation: A diagnosis list does not establish the products currently taken.
rationales: Missing documentation does not prove absence.
Current medicines still need to be established.
The same diagnosis can have different medication histories.
units.hint: Do diagnoses specify every product taken?

units.title: Consent is a discussion · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: A viva answer treats a signed form as the entire informed-consent process. What is the best correction?
choices: A signature alone guarantees understanding
Discussion of information, alternatives and choice also matters
Documentation replaces the need for questions
units.explanation: A signature documents part of the process; information and informed choice remain essential.
rationales: Understanding cannot be inferred from a signature alone.
A record does not replace discussion.

units.title: Separate patient and procedure risk · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Two paper cases share a medicine but differ in medical history and planned procedure. Which comparison is defensible?
choices: Consider the patient and procedure factors in each case
Assign identical risk from the medicine name alone
Ignore the procedure if the medicine is recorded
units.explanation: A shared medicine does not make individual or procedure risks identical.

units.title: Explain haemostasis · apply
units.lesson: Close the notes. Apply the concept to this new example, then compare your reasoning with the explanation.
units.question: Which pairing correctly distinguishes the platelet and coagulation contributions?
choices: Platelets form fibrin directly; coagulation forms the cells
Platelets contribute the initial plug; coagulation generates fibrin
Both terms refer to the same material
units.explanation: Platelet aggregation and fibrin generation are distinct interacting components.
rationales: This reverses and confuses the contributions.
units.hint: Identify the plug and its reinforcement.
